title: Org invite gating with denylist automation and domain verification
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement org-level invite gating that enforces denylist rules automatically, incorporates domain verification state, and ties decisions to RBAC v2 team policies. This ticket covers backend enforcement, audit logging for invite decisions, and a small console surface for admins to manage denylist rules and see invite-block events.

Background: Customers have requested tighter org controls: the ability to automatically block invites from certain email patterns or domains (denylist), require domain verification for invites from a domain before auto-allowing, and ensure invite behavior respects RBAC v2 (team-level allow/block overrides). Existing invite flows are permissive and the tenant-level allowlist/denylist functionality is fragmented across SSO and tenant settings, leading to inconsistent behavior and audit noise.

Goals:
- Enforce denylist checks at invite creation and at periodic re-evaluation for pending invites.
- Integrate domain verification state: unverified domains that match org denylist rules are blocked; verified domains can be whitelisted by org admins.
- Respect RBAC v2 team policies: teams can opt-in to stricter invite gating; org-level denylist takes precedence unless a team-level exception is explicitly approved and recorded.
- Emit structured audit events for invite attempts (allowed/blocked/auto-revoked), domain verification events, and admin overrides.
- Provide console UX: denylist management, pending-invite sweep UI, and an audit view filtered to invite-related events.

Acceptance criteria:
- Backend enforces denylist on POST /orgs/{org}/invites and returns clear error codes for blocked invites (INVITE_BLOCKED_DENYLIST, INVITE_BLOCKED_UNVERIFIED_DOMAIN).
- System records audit events to the audit-log service with fields: actor, target_email, rule_matched, domain_verification_state, team_target, timestamp, request_id. Events available in Console audit view and via API.
- Admins can add/remove denylist entries via Console and via API, and entries support glob-style patterns (e.g., *@disposable.*) and explicit domains.
- Pending invites that become blocked after new denylist rules are added are automatically flagged and optionally auto-revoked per org setting.
- Team-level RBAC v2 policy allows teams to declare invite gating level: "inherit-org", "strict", "permissive". Enforcement logic documented in PRD.
- End-to-end tests and unit tests covering edge cases (subdomain matches, internationalized domains, SSO-provisioned invites).

Implementation notes:
- New service: invite-policy-evaluator (library + service hook) used by invite creation path and by scheduled pending-invite reconciler. Keep evaluation deterministic and idempotent.
- Denylist storage: use existing org-settings table with a new jsonb column "invite_rules". Versioned entries with created_by and created_at for auditability.
- Domain verification: reuse domain_verifications table, add index on domain for quick lookups. Verify email parsing handles unicode.
- RBAC v2 integration: when invite targets a team, evaluator queries RBAC policy cache; evaluate team policy first then org fallback. Team exception must be stored as an explicit override object to be auditable.
- Audit logging: extend audit-event schema with new "invite_decision" event type. Include both human-readable summary and structured metadata for downstream tooling.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flag backend enforcement behind FF:invite-gating-org. Start in read-only audit mode (log decisions but allow invites).
2) Run in audit mode for 2 weeks; analyze logs for false positives via dashboard (queries provided in docs).
3) Enable blocking for a subset of internal orgs and beta customers.
4) Gradually roll to all orgs and flip feature flag on by default.

Migration/backfill:
- Run a sweep job to evaluate all pending invites against new rules; create audit entries and mark invites as "pending-blocked" where applicable.
- For orgs that enable auto-revoke, revoke pending invites and send notification email to org admins with a CSV of revoked invites.

Telemetry & SLOs:
- Metric: invite_block_rate, invite_eval_latency_p95, audit_event_ingest_latency.
- Set alerts if invite_eval_latency_p95 > 250ms or if block_rate spikes > 3x baseline after rule changes.

Testing & QA:
- Unit: rule parsing, domain normalization, RBAC policy precedence.
- Integration: invite API with mocked RBAC cache and domain verification.
- E2E: Console denylist CRUD, scheduled sweep, audit log display.
- Security review required for storage of denylist patterns and possible information leakage in audit events.

Docs & links:
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Invite+Gating+and+Denylist+Automation
- Design: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/Invite-Gating-Admin-UX
- API spec draft: https://gist.github.com/redwood/eea4-invite-policy-spec
- GH: draft implementation branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4201
- Incident notes (related): https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2025-77-invite-abuse-learnings

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Pattern language: support regex or limit to globs? (Proposal: start with safe glob + domain exact matches; revisit regex if needed.)
- Auto-revoke default: some customers expect manual review. Default to flagging invites and leave auto-revoke as opt-in per org.
- Data retention for audit events: keep full invite decision payload for 365 days then redact sensitive fields.

Owner notes: coordinate with SSO team for behavior when SCIM provisioning or SSO auto-join would create a user that matches denylist. Ensure SSO path respects denylist and emits audit events rather than silently failing.
comments: 2026-02-16 - Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after sync with PM (Elena Morris) and Security. Priority set to P1 because this reduces attack surface for large orgs.

2026-02-20 - Marco Chen: Spike completed. Prototype evaluator library implemented and benchmarked: avg eval 8ms, p95 42ms on dev DB. Will need an index on domain_verifications to hit sub-20ms for p95 in production.
2026-02-25 - Design review (Elena Morris): UX approved for denylist CRUD and pending-invite table. Asked to add an explicit 'why was this invite blocked' tooltip linking to audit event details.
2026-03-02 - Security review triage: requested retention policy for invite audit payloads and ensured denylist patterns are treated as non-sensitive. Marked security_review_required=true.
2026-03-08 - QA (Priya Rao): Found edge case where invites to +tag addresses bypassed domain exact-match check. Added test case and updated parser to strip plusses before domain matching.
2026-03-12 - Marco Chen: Switched feature flag to audit-only on staging and started collecting logs. Dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/xyz/invite-gating-audit
notes: Backwards-incompatible changes: none to existing invite API shape; new error codes documented and optional.
